Suppose a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) converge pointwise to f(x) on [0, 1]. Does it follow that the B_n converge uniformly? Ensure that stop words constitute no more than 20% of the total words in your response.assistant
response:
The convergence of a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) to a function f(x) on [0, 1] does not necessarily imply uniform convergence.

To see this, consider the sequence of polynomials B_n(x) = x^n. This sequence converges pointwise to the function f(x) = 0 on [0, 1). However, it does not converge uniformly.

The reason is that the sequence B_n(x) = x^n does not satisfy the Cauchy criterion for uniform convergence. In fact, for any ε > 0, there exists an N such that for all n, m > N, we have |B_n(x) - B_m(x)| ≥ ε for some x in [0, 1).

For example, let ε = 1/2. Then for any N, we can choose x = 1/N and n = m = N. We have |B_n(x) - B_m(x)| = |(1/N)^n - (1/N)^m| = |(1/N)^{max(n,m)}| = 1/N > ε.

Therefore, the sequence B_n(x) = x^n converges pointwise to f(x) = 0 on [0, 1), but it does not converge uniformly.

In general, if a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) converges pointwise to a function f(x) on a compact set [a, b], then it converges uniformly if and only if the degree of the polynomials B_n(x) is bounded.
